sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca etac chrutvā mahārāja bhāradvājasya dhīmataḥ anumānya tam ācāryaṃ prāyāc chāradvataṃ prati
english: Saṃjaya said: Having heard these words of the wise son of Bharadvāja, O great king, and having taken leave of that teacher, he went toward the son of Śaradvat.

sanskrit: so 'bhivādya kṛpaṃ rājā kṛtvā cāpi pradakṣiṇam uvāca durdharṣatamaṃ vākyaṃ vākyaviśāradaḥ
english: Saluting Kṛpa and walking around him in reverence, that king, skilled in speech, spoke this word to the most unassailable of men.

sanskrit: anumānaye tvāṃ yotsyāmi guro vigatakalmaṣaḥ jayeyaṃ ca ripūn sarvān anujñātas tvayānagha
english: I ask your leave, O teacher; I shall fight, freed of all blame. With your sanction, O sinless one, may I conquer all my foes.

sanskrit: kṛpa uvāca yadi māṃ nābhigacchethā yuddhāya kṛtaniścayaḥ śapeyaṃ tvāṃ mahārāja parābhāvāya sarvaśaḥ
english: Kṛpa said: Had you not come to me, resolved upon the battle, I would have cursed you, O great king, to utter ruin in every way.

sanskrit: arthasya puruṣo dāso dāsas tv artho na kasya cit iti satyaṃ mahārāja baddho 'smy arthena kauravaiḥ
english: A man is the slave of wealth, but wealth is no man's slave. That is the truth, O great king: I am bound by wealth to the Kauravas.

sanskrit: teṣām arthe mahārāja yoddhavyam iti me matiḥ atas tvāṃ klībavad brūmi yuddhād anyat kim icchasi
english: For their sake I must fight—such is my resolve, O great king. Therefore I speak to you like one unmanned: what do you wish, other than battle?

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca hanta pṛcchāmi te tasmād ācārya śṛṇu me vacaḥ
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: Then come, I shall ask you, O teacher; hear my words.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca ity uktvā vyathito rājā novāca gatacetanaḥ taṃ gautamaḥ pratyuvāca vijñāyāsya vivakṣitam avadhyo 'haṃ mahīpāla yudhyasva jayam āpnuhi
english: Saṃjaya said: Having spoken thus, the king grew troubled and, his senses faltering, said nothing more. But the descendant of Gotama, perceiving what he meant to ask, answered him: I cannot be slain, O lord of earth; fight, and win the victory.

sanskrit: prītas tv abhigamenāhaṃ jayaṃ tava narādhipa āśāsiṣye sadotthāya satyam etad bravīmi te
english: Pleased by your coming, O ruler of men, I shall ever rise up and pray for your victory. This truth I tell you.

sanskrit: etac chrutvā mahārāja gautamasya vacas tadā anumānya kṛpaṃ rājā prayayau yena madrarāṭ
english: Having heard these words of the descendant of Gotama, O great king, and having taken leave of Kṛpa, the king went on toward the lord of the Madras.

sanskrit: sa śalyam abhivādyātha kṛtvā cābhipradakṣiṇam uvāca rājā durdharṣam ātmaniḥśreyasaṃ vacaḥ
english: Then, saluting Śalya and walking around him in reverence, the king spoke to that unassailable one a word that sought his own highest good.

sanskrit: anumānaye tvāṃ yotsyāmi guro vigatakalmaṣaḥ jayeyaṃ ca mahārāja anujñātas tvayā ripūn
english: I ask your leave, O teacher; I shall fight, freed of all blame. With your sanction, O great king, may I conquer my foes.

sanskrit: śalya uvāca yadi māṃ nābhigacchethā yuddhāya kṛtaniścayaḥ śapeyaṃ tvāṃ mahārāja parābhāvāya vai raṇe
english: Śalya said: Had you not come to me, resolved upon the battle, I would have cursed you, O great king, to defeat in the field.

sanskrit: tuṣṭo 'smi pūjitaś cāsmi yat kāṅkṣasi tad astu te anujānāmi caiva tvāṃ yudhyasva jayam āpnuhi
english: I am pleased, and I am honored; let what you desire be yours. I grant you leave: fight, and win the victory.

sanskrit: brūhi caiva paraṃ vīra kenārthaḥ kiṃ dadāmi te evaṃ gate mahārāja yuddhād anyat kim icchasi
english: Speak further, O hero: what do you need, what shall I give you? Things being as they are, O great king, what do you wish, other than battle?

sanskrit: arthasya puruṣo dāso dāsas tv artho na kasya cit iti satyaṃ mahārāja baddho 'smy arthena kauravaiḥ
english: A man is the slave of wealth, but wealth is no man's slave. That is the truth, O great king: I am bound by wealth to the Kauravas.

sanskrit: kariṣyāmi hi te kāmaṃ bhāgineya yathepsitam bravīmy ataḥ klībavat tvāṃ yuddhād anyat kim icchasi
english: I shall fulfill your desire as you wish it, O sister's son. Therefore I speak to you like one unmanned: what do you wish, other than battle?

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca mantrayasva mahārāja nityaṃ maddhitam uttamam kāmaṃ yudhya parasyārthe varam etad vṛṇomy aham
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: Counsel me always toward my highest good, O great king. Fight, if you must, for the enemy's sake—this is the boon I choose.

sanskrit: śalya uvāca brūhi kim atra sāhyaṃ te karomi nṛpasattama kāmaṃ yotsye parasyārthe vṛto 'smy arthena kauravaiḥ
english: Śalya said: Tell me what help I may render you here, O best of kings. I shall fight, if I must, for the enemy's sake, for I have been bought by the Kauravas with wealth.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca sa eva me varaḥ satya udyoge yas tvayā kṛtaḥ sūtaputrasya saṃgrāme kāryas tejovadhas tvayā
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: That very promise you made me during the preparations is my boon, in truth: in battle you must break the fire and spirit of the charioteer's son.

sanskrit: śalya uvāca saṃpatsyaty eṣa te kāmaḥ kuntīputra yathepsitaḥ gaccha yudhyasva visrabdhaṃ pratijāne jayaṃ tava
english: Śalya said: This desire of yours shall be fulfilled as you wish it, O son of Kuntī. Go, fight without fear; I pledge you your victory.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca anumānyātha kaunteyo mātulaṃ madrakeśvaram nirjagāma mahāsainyād bhrātṛbhiḥ parivāritaḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: Then the son of Kuntī, having taken leave of his maternal uncle, the lord of the Madrakas, went forth from the great host, surrounded by his brothers.

sanskrit: vāsudevas tu rādheyam āhave 'bhijagāma vai tata enam uvācedaṃ pāṇḍavārthe gadāgrajaḥ
english: But Vāsudeva approached the son of Rādhā upon the field, and then the elder brother of Gada spoke to him thus, for the Pāṇḍavas' sake:

sanskrit: śrutaṃ me karṇa bhīṣmasya dveṣāt kila na yotsyasi asmān varaya rādheya yāvad bhīṣmo na hanyate
english: I have heard, Karṇa, that out of enmity toward Bhīṣma you will not fight. Choose our side, O son of Rādhā, so long as Bhīṣma is not slain.

sanskrit: hate tu bhīṣme rādheya punar eṣyasi saṃyuge dhārtarāṣṭrasya sāhāyyaṃ yadi paśyasi cet samam
english: And when Bhīṣma is slain, O son of Rādhā, you may return again to the battle to aid the son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, if you deem it fair and fitting.

sanskrit: karṇa uvāca na vipriyaṃ kariṣyāmi dhārtarāṣṭrasya keśava tyaktaprāṇaṃ hi māṃ viddhi duryodhanahitaiṣiṇam
english: Karṇa said: I shall do nothing displeasing to the son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, O Keśava. Know that I have laid down my very life as one who seeks Duryodhana's good.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca tac chrutvā vacanaṃ kṛṣṇaḥ saṃnyavartata bhārata yudhiṣṭhirapurogaiś ca pāṇḍavaiḥ saha saṃgataḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: Hearing that word, Kṛṣṇa turned back, O descendant of Bharata, and rejoined the Pāṇḍavas, with Yudhiṣṭhira at their head.

sanskrit: atha sainyasya madhye tu prākrośat pāṇḍavāgrajaḥ yo 'smān vṛṇoti tad ahaṃ varaye sāhyakāraṇāt
english: Then in the midst of the host the eldest of the Pāṇḍavas proclaimed aloud: Whoever chooses us, him I in turn choose, for the sake of his aid.

sanskrit: atha tān samabhiprekṣya yuyutsur idam abravīt prītātmā dharmarājānaṃ kuntīputraṃ yudhiṣṭhiram
english: Then, looking upon them, Yuyutsu, his heart gladdened, said this to the King of Righteousness, Yudhiṣṭhira the son of Kuntī:

sanskrit: ahaṃ yotsyāmi miṣataḥ saṃyuge dhārtarāṣṭrajān yuṣmadarthe mahārāja yadi māṃ vṛṇuṣe 'nagha
english: I shall fight, before his very eyes, the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra in the battle, for your cause, O great king, if you will choose me, O sinless one.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca ehy ehi sarve yotsyāmas tava bhrātṝn apaṇḍitān yuyutso vāsudevaś ca vayaṃ ca brūma sarvaśaḥ
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: Come, come! We shall all fight your foolish brothers. Yuyutsu, both Vāsudeva and we say so with one accord.

sanskrit: vṛṇomi tvāṃ mahābāho yudhyasva mama kāraṇāt tvayi piṇḍaś ca tantuś ca dhṛtarāṣṭrasya dṛśyate
english: I choose you, O mighty-armed one; fight for my sake. In you alone are seen the funeral offering and the continuing line of Dhṛtarāṣṭra.

sanskrit: bhajasvāsmān rājaputra bhajamānān mahādyute na bhaviṣyati durbuddhir dhārtarāṣṭro 'tyamarṣaṇaḥ
english: Cleave to us, O prince of splendor, who cleave to you. The evil-minded, overbearing son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra shall not endure.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca tato yuyutsuḥ kauravyaḥ parityajya sutāṃs tava jagāma pāṇḍuputrāṇāṃ senāṃ viśrāvya dundubhim
english: Saṃjaya said: Then Yuyutsu of the Kuru race, forsaking your sons, went over to the army of the sons of Pāṇḍu, sounding the war-drum as he went.

sanskrit: tato yudhiṣṭhiro rājā saṃprahṛṣṭaḥ sahānujaiḥ jagrāha kavacaṃ bhūyo dīptimat kanakojjvalam
english: Then King Yudhiṣṭhira, greatly rejoicing along with his younger brothers, once more took up his radiant armor, bright with gold.

sanskrit: pratyapadyanta te sarve rathān svān puruṣarṣabhāḥ tato vyūhaṃ yathāpūrvaṃ pratyavyūhanta te punaḥ
english: All those bulls among men mounted again their several chariots, and then they once more arrayed their battle-formation as it had been before.

sanskrit: avādayan dundubhīṃś ca śataśaś caiva puṣkarān siṃhanādāṃś ca vividhān vineduḥ puruṣarṣabhāḥ
english: They sounded their war-drums and kettledrums by the hundreds, and those bulls among men raised lion-roars of many kinds.

sanskrit: rathasthān puruṣavyāghrān pāṇḍavān prekṣya pārthivāḥ dhṛṣṭadyumnādayaḥ sarve punar jahṛṣire mudā
english: Beholding the Pāṇḍavas, those tigers among men, standing upon their chariots, the kings led by Dhṛṣṭadyumna all rejoiced again with gladness.

sanskrit: gauravaṃ pāṇḍuputrāṇāṃ mānyān mānayatāṃ ca tān dṛṣṭvā mahīkṣitas tatra pūjayāṃ cakrire bhṛśam
english: Seeing the dignity of the sons of Pāṇḍu, who honored those worthy of honor, the rulers of earth there praised them exceedingly.

sanskrit: sauhṛdaṃ ca kṛpāṃ caiva prāptakālaṃ mahātmanām dayāṃ ca jñātiṣu parāṃ kathayāṃ cakrire nṛpāḥ
english: And the kings spoke of the friendship and the compassion of those great souls, timely as it was, and of their supreme tenderness toward their kinsmen.

sanskrit: sādhu sādhv iti sarvatra niśceruḥ stutisaṃhitāḥ vācaḥ puṇyāḥ kīrtimatāṃ manohṛdayaharṣiṇīḥ
english: "Well done, well done!" rang out on every side—holy words of praise from men of renown, gladdening the mind and the heart.

sanskrit: mlecchāś cāryāś ca ye tatra dadṛśuḥ śuśruvus tadā vṛttaṃ tat pāṇḍuputrāṇāṃ rurudus te sagadgadāḥ
english: The barbarians and the noble Āryas who there saw and heard of that conduct of the sons of Pāṇḍu wept then, their voices choked with feeling.

sanskrit: tato jaghnur mahābherīḥ śataśaś caiva puṣkarān śaṅkhāṃś ca gokṣīranibhān dadhmur hṛṣṭā manasvinaḥ
english: Then those high-spirited men, full of joy, beat their great war-drums and kettledrums by the hundreds, and blew their conches white as cow's milk.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca evaṃ vyūḍheṣv anīkeṣu māmakeṣv itareṣu ca ke pūrvaṃ prāharaṃs tatra kuravaḥ pāṇḍavās tathā
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: When the armies were thus arrayed, both mine and the others', who struck the first blow there—the Kurus or the Pāṇḍavas?

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca bhrātṛbhiḥ sahito rājan putro duryodhanas tava bhīṣmaṃ pramukhataḥ kṛtvā prayayau saha senayā
english: Saṃjaya said: Together with his brothers, O king, your son Duryodhana, placing Bhīṣma at the head, advanced with his army.

sanskrit: tathaiva pāṇḍavāḥ sarve bhīmasenapurogamāḥ bhīṣmeṇa yuddham icchantaḥ prayayur hṛṣṭamānasāḥ
english: Likewise all the Pāṇḍavas, with Bhīmasena at their head, eager for battle with Bhīṣma, advanced with gladdened hearts.

sanskrit: kṣveḍāḥ kilakilāśabdāḥ krakacā goviṣāṇikāḥ bherīmṛdaṅgamurajā hayakuñjaranisvanāḥ
english: Roars and shrill clamoring cries, krakaca trumpets and cow-horn pipes, kettledrums, tabors, and drums, the neighing of horses and the trumpeting of elephants—

sanskrit: ubhayoḥ senayo rājaṃs tatas te 'smān samādravan vayaṃ pratinadantaś ca tadāsīt tumulaṃ mahat
english: —rose from both armies, O king. Then they charged at us, and we roared back in answer; and at that there arose a vast tumult.

sanskrit: mahānty anīkāni mahāsamucchraye; samāgame pāṇḍavadhārtarāṣṭrayoḥ cakampire śaṅkhamṛdaṅganisvanaiḥ; prakampitānīva vanāni vāyunā
english: At that great upheaval, in the clash of the Pāṇḍavas and the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, the mighty hosts trembled at the blasts of conches and drums, like forests shaken by the wind.

sanskrit: narendranāgāśvarathākulānām; abhyāyatīnām aśive muhūrte babhūva ghoṣas tumulaś camūnāṃ; vātoddhutānām iva sāgarāṇām
english: As the armies, thronged with kings and elephants, horses and chariots, advanced in that inauspicious hour, there arose a tumultuous roar of the hosts, like that of oceans churned by the gale.

sanskrit: tasmin samutthite śabde tumule lomaharṣaṇe bhīmaseno mahābāhuḥ prāṇadad govṛṣo yathā
english: As that tumultuous, hair-raising din arose, the mighty-armed Bhīmasena bellowed like a bull.

sanskrit: śaṅkhadundubhinirghoṣaṃ vāraṇānāṃ ca bṛṃhitam siṃhanādaṃ ca sainyānāṃ bhīmasenaravo 'bhyabhūt
english: The blare of conches and drums, the trumpeting of elephants, and the lion-roars of the troops—all these the roar of Bhīmasena overwhelmed.

sanskrit: hayānāṃ heṣamāṇānām anīkeṣu sahasraśaḥ sarvān abhyabhavac chabdān bhīmasenasya nisvanaḥ
english: Over the neighing of horses in their thousands throughout the ranks, the cry of Bhīmasena rose above every other sound.

sanskrit: taṃ śrutvā ninadaṃ tasya sainyās tava vitatrasuḥ jīmūtasyeva nadataḥ śakrāśanisamasvanam
english: Hearing that roar of his, loud as a thundercloud and ringing like Indra's bolt, your soldiers were stricken with terror.

sanskrit: vāhanāni ca sarvāṇi śakṛnmūtraṃ prasusruvuḥ śabdena tasya vīrasya siṃhasyevetare mṛgāḥ
english: And all the beasts of burden voided their dung and urine at that hero's cry, as lesser creatures do at the roar of a lion.

sanskrit: darśayan ghoram ātmānaṃ mahābhram iva nādayan vibhīṣayaṃs tava sutāṃs tava senāṃ samabhyayāt
english: Showing himself in dreadful form, roaring like a great storm-cloud, terrifying your sons, he bore down upon your army.

sanskrit: tam āyāntaṃ maheṣvāsaṃ sodaryāḥ paryavārayan chādayantaḥ śaravrātair meghā iva divākaram
english: As that great archer came on, his own brothers surrounded him, covering him with showers of arrows as clouds veil the sun.

sanskrit: duryodhanaś ca putras te durmukho duḥsahaḥ śalaḥ duḥśāsanaś cātirathas tathā durmarṣaṇo nṛpa
english: There were Duryodhana your son, and Durmukha, Duḥsaha, Śala, Duḥśāsana the mighty car-warrior, and Durmarṣaṇa too, O king,

sanskrit: viviṃśatiś citraseno vikarṇaś ca mahārathaḥ purumitro jayo bhojaḥ saumadattiś ca vīryavān
english: Viviṃśati, Citrasena, and Vikarṇa the great car-warrior, Purumitra, Jaya, Bhoja, and the valiant son of Somadatta.

sanskrit: mahācāpāni dhunvanto jaladā iva vidyutaḥ ādadānāś ca nārācān nirmuktāśīviṣopamān
english: Brandishing their great bows like storm-clouds flashing lightning, and taking up iron shafts like vipers darting forth from their holes,

sanskrit: atha tān draupadīputrāḥ saubhadraś ca mahārathaḥ nakulaḥ sahadevaś ca dhṛṣṭadyumnaś ca pārṣataḥ
english: Against them the sons of Draupadī, and the son of Subhadrā that great car-warrior, and Nakula and Sahadeva, and Dhṛṣṭadyumna the grandson of Pṛṣata,

sanskrit: dhārtarāṣṭrān pratiyayur ardayantaḥ śitaiḥ śaraiḥ vajrair iva mahāvegaiḥ śikharāṇi dharābhṛtām
english: advanced against the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, harrowing them with sharp arrows as thunderbolts of great force shatter the peaks of mountains.

sanskrit: tasmin prathamasaṃmarde bhīmajyātalanisvane tāvakānāṃ pareṣāṃ ca nāsīt kaś cit parāṅmukhaḥ
english: In that first onset, amid the dreadful twang of bowstrings against bracers, not one of yours nor of the foe turned his face from the fight.

sanskrit: lāghavaṃ droṇaśiṣyāṇām apaśyaṃ bharatarṣabha nimittavedhināṃ rājañ śarān utsṛjatāṃ bhṛśam
english: I beheld the deftness of Droṇa's pupils, O bull of the Bharatas—marksmen who struck their targets unfailingly, loosing their arrows in dense streams, O king.

sanskrit: nopaśāmyati nirghoṣo dhanuṣāṃ kūjatāṃ tathā viniśceruḥ śarā dīptā jyotīṃṣīva nabhastalāt
english: The din of the twanging bows did not cease, and blazing arrows shot forth like meteors falling from the vault of heaven.

sanskrit: sarve tv anye mahīpālāḥ prekṣakā iva bhārata dadṛśur darśanīyaṃ taṃ bhīmaṃ jñātisamāgamam
english: But all the other rulers of earth, like mere spectators, O descendant of Bharata, looked on at that dreadful yet wondrous clash of kinsmen.

sanskrit: tatas te jātasaṃrambhāḥ parasparakṛtāgasaḥ anyonyaspardhayā rājan vyāyacchanta mahārathāḥ
english: Then those great car-warriors, their fury kindled, each having wronged the other, strove against one another in rivalry, O king.

sanskrit: kurupāṇḍavasene te hastyaśvarathasaṃkule śuśubhāte raṇe 'tīva paṭe citragate iva
english: The hosts of the Kurus and the Pāṇḍavas, thronged with elephants, horses, and chariots, shone exceedingly upon the field, like a painting wrought upon a canvas.

sanskrit: tatas te pārthivāḥ sarve pragṛhītaśarāsanāḥ sahasainyāḥ samāpetuḥ putrasya tava śāsanāt
english: Then all those kings, with bows grasped firm, fell upon the foe together with their troops, at your son's command.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhireṇa cādiṣṭāḥ pārthivās te sahasraśaḥ vinadantaḥ samāpetuḥ putrasya tava vāhinīm
english: And the kings, by their thousands, commanded by Yudhiṣṭhira, rushed roaring upon your son's host.

sanskrit: ubhayoḥ senayos tīvraḥ sainyānāṃ sa samāgamaḥ antardhīyata cādityaḥ sainyena rajasāvṛtaḥ
english: Fierce was that meeting of the troops of both armies; and the sun was hidden away, the host shrouded in dust.

sanskrit: prayuddhānāṃ prabhagnānāṃ punarāvartatām api nātra sveṣāṃ pareṣāṃ vā viśeṣaḥ samajāyata
english: Among those who fought, those who broke and fled, and those who rallied again, no distinction could be made there between one's own men and the foe.

sanskrit: tasmiṃs tu tumule yuddhe vartamāne mahābhaye ati sarvāṇy anīkāni pitā te 'bhivyarocata
english: And as that tumultuous, terrible battle raged, your father shone forth surpassing all the hosts.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca pūrvāhṇe tasya raudrasya yuddham ahno viśāṃ pate prāvartata mahāghoraṃ rājñāṃ dehāvakartanam
english: Saṃjaya said: In the forenoon of that fearful day, O lord of peoples, there began a most dreadful battle, the hewing-asunder of the bodies of kings.

sanskrit: kurūṇāṃ pāṇḍavānāṃ ca saṃgrāme vijigīṣatām siṃhānām iva saṃhrādo divam urvīṃ ca nādayan
english: From the Kurus and the Pāṇḍavas, longing for victory in the fray, there rose a roar like that of lions, making heaven and earth resound.

sanskrit: āsīt kilakilāśabdas talaśaṅkharavaiḥ saha jajñire siṃhanādāś ca śūrāṇāṃ pratigarjatām
english: There were shrill clamoring cries mingled with the clap of palms and the blare of conches, and the lion-roars of heroes bellowing back at one another arose.

sanskrit: talatrābhihatāś caiva jyāśabdā bharatarṣabha pattīnāṃ pādaśabdāś ca vājināṃ ca mahāsvanāḥ
english: There was the twang of bowstrings struck by the leather guards, O bull of the Bharatas, the tread of foot-soldiers, and the loud neighing of horses,

sanskrit: tottrāṅkuśanipātāś ca āyudhānāṃ ca nisvanāḥ ghaṇṭāśabdāś ca nāgānām anyonyam abhidhāvatām
english: the fall of goads and elephant-hooks, the clash of weapons, and the ringing of the bells of elephants as they charged against one another.

sanskrit: tasmin samudite śabde tumule lomaharṣaṇe babhūva rathanirghoṣaḥ parjanyaninadopamaḥ
english: As that tumultuous, hair-raising din arose, the rumble of chariots became like the thunder of a rain-cloud.

sanskrit: te manaḥ krūram ādhāya samabhityaktajīvitāḥ pāṇḍavān abhyavartanta sarva evocchritadhvajāḥ
english: Setting their minds upon cruelty and casting their lives utterly aside, they all, with banners raised on high, bore down upon the Pāṇḍavas.
